own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = E (1 - exp(-t/RC)), tau = RC = 5000*20e-6 = 0.1 s

T3BCA.regime: the disconnection time matters only if it is earlier than 80 ms; 400 ms is later

T3ED2.regime: the disconnection time matters only if it is earlier than 80 ms; 400 ms is later

defect_reasons.other: TE931 ('cut off from the battery') does not say whether the circuit is left open (capacitor holds 5.414 V) or the battery is replaced by a conducting path (capacitor discharges through the resistor), though the open-circuit reading is the natural one.

notes: Base: 12(1 - e^-0.8) = 12(1 - 0.44933) = 6.608 V. Disconnected at 60 ms with an ideal capacitor held open: 12(1 - e^-0.6) = 12(0.45119) = 5.414 V. Extra 3.5 kOhm in series: tau = 8500*20e-6 = 0.17 s, 12(1 - e^-0.4706) = 12(1 - 0.62464) = 4.504 V. Resistors inserted and removed before the connection (TC38C, T61C2) leave no trace on an uncharged capacitor, so no path to the target in the experiment as run; I class them D (could also be viewed as a temporal invariance). Variant check: T0ED4, T61C2, TE7F1, T68E7 all 3.5 kOhm; TE931 and T8648 both 60 ms; T3ED2 and T3BCA both 400 ms; the 60 ms and 400 ms sentences differ in number (presumably R vs K versions of the same timing quantity). TC38C and T4C87 say 'small resistor' with no number. Assumed the capacitor does not leak after the circuit is opened (standard idealisation).
